bottleneck: Prime editing can write insertions, deletions, and replacements without double-strand breaks, but its efficiency drops sharply in many primary and therapeutically relevant cell types. The mechanism requires a pegRNA, reverse transcriptase, and nickase to coordinate, and in non-dividing or hard-to-transfect cells the edit rate falls below therapeutic thresholds. Optimizing pegRNA design remains partly empirical.
current_state: Efficiency is improving in cell lines, but delivery of the large prime editor complex in vivo and consistent performance across tissues remain unsolved. Clinical applications are still preclinical.

title: Prime editing efficiency collapses in primary cells
why_it_blocks: Prime editing is the most versatile editor, but versatility without efficiency is unusable in patients. Low in vivo rates force the field back toward simpler, riskier nucleases for the edits prime editing was meant to make safe.
